text: The predicate requires B(x,x)>0 for every nonzero rational vector, exactly positive definiteness of the associated quadratic form in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3). The lattice supplies finite-dimensionality, but the definition imposes no redundant nondegeneracy premise. Rank zero satisfies the universal condition. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RankOne/Basic.lean#L196) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Signature.lean#L195) passes.
The rank-one predicate is exactly a>0.
The elementwise inequality quantifies over the full rational space.

This is the maximal dimension of a rational subspace where−B(x,x) is positive definite. By [Mathlib’s inertia definitions and Sylvester theorem](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Signature.lean#L65), it counts the negative coefficients in any orthogonal diagonalization. The full lattice makes the ambient space finite-dimensional, so the upstream infinite-dimensional default is irrelevant. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L319) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L291) passes.
The negative rank-one example has negative index1.
The hyperbolic plane has one positive and one negative index.

The value is dimℚ ker B, so it counts the zero directions in the inertia decomposition of [Mathlib’s inertia definitions and Sylvester theorem](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Signature.lean#L65). It measures the radical, not all isotropic vectors: a nondegenerate indefinite form can have nonzero isotropic vectors while this index is0. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L342) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L291) passes.
The affine example has null index1.
The indefinite hyperbolic plane has null index0.

The value is the maximal dimension of a subspace on which B(x,x) is positive definite. The full carrier supplies finite-dimensionality, and [Mathlib’s inertia definitions and Sylvester theorem](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Signature.lean#L65) identifies this maximum with the number of positive diagonal coefficients. It is a rational-space invariant, not a count of positive lattice vectors. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RankOne/Basic.lean#L178) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L342) passes.
A positive rank-one form has positive index1.
The degenerate semidefinite example still has positive index1.

This is nonnegativity of the symmetric rational form: B(x,x)≥0 for every vector. Symmetry is already part of the lattice structure, so the bundled bilinear predicate agrees with the usual semidefinite notion in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3). It allows a nonzero radical. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L329) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L336) passes.
The degenerate affine form is semidefinite.
The same example proves semidefinite does not imply nondegenerate.

In an orthogonal diagonalization, semidefiniteness excludes negative coefficients and nondegeneracy excludes zero coefficients. All remaining coefficients are positive, and conversely a positive definite form has both properties. This is the finite-dimensional consequence of [Mathlib’s inertia definitions and Sylvester theorem](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Signature.lean#L65), applied to the symmetric rational form. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L329) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L336) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RankOne/Basic.lean#L196) passes.
The affine form satisfies only semidefiniteness.
Its radical explains why the nondegeneracy conjunct cannot be omitted.
The rank-one criterion is strict positivity of a.

The tuple is explicitly (positive index, radical dimension, negative index). These are the three inertia counts of [Mathlib’s inertia definitions and Sylvester theorem](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Signature.lean#L65). Dolgachev orders the null count last; Lean documents its own order and consistently puts it in the middle, including degenerate forms. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L291) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L319) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L342) passes.
The indefinite nondegenerate example is (1,0,1).
The negative rank-one example is (0,0,1).
The affine degenerate example is (1,1,0).

Orthogonal diagonalization divides the basis coefficients into positive, zero and negative entries. Their counts sum to the dimension, exactly the decomposition in [Mathlib’s inertia definitions and Sylvester theorem](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Signature.lean#L65). The carrier rank equals this rational dimension because the lattice is full; degeneracy contributes through the middle count. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L342) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L291) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Basic.lean#L124) passes.
The affine example gives1+1+0=2.
The hyperbolic example gives1+0+1=2.
Integral carrier rank equals rational ambient dimension.

Strict positivity for every nonzero vector gives nonnegativity there, and bilinearity gives B(0,0)=0. Hence positive definiteness implies semidefiniteness exactly as defined in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3), including the zero-dimensional case. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Signature.lean#L250) passes.
The stronger characterization also records the nondegeneracy consequence.

Viewing B as x↦B(x,·), kernel membership says that this functional is zero. Equality with the zero functional is precisely vanishing on every rational y, giving the stated characterization of the radical used in [Mathlib’s inertia definitions and Sylvester theorem](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Signature.lean#L65). The test is not merely B(x,x)=0. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L374) passes.
In the affine model the radical is exactly x₀−x₁=0.

The kernel of x↦B(x,·) is exactly the set annihilating every vector under B. Symmetry makes the left and right radicals agree. This is the null space in the inertia decomposition of [Mathlib’s inertia definitions and Sylvester theorem](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Signature.lean#L65); it differs from the isotropic cone. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Signature.lean#L72) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L374) passes.
Membership tests all pairings.
The affine example computes the actual kernel.

For Q(x)=B(x,x), symmetry gives polar(Q)=2B. Over ℚ,2 is invertible, so the quadratic radical equals ker B. This matches the radical used by [Mathlib’s inertia definitions and Sylvester theorem](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Signature.lean#L65); the statement does not transfer that identity to characteristic2. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Norm.lean#L163) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L374) passes.
The norm polarization is exactly2 times the bilinear pairing.
The affine radical is the expected diagonal subspace.

The predicate is positive definiteness of−B(x,x), equivalently B(x,x)<0 on every nonzero vector. This is exactly negative definiteness in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3). It uses the self-pairing without dividing by2 and permits the vacuous rank-zero case. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RankOne/Basic.lean#L204) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Signature.lean#L220) passes.
For rank one this means a<0.
The full rational-space inequality is exposed explicitly.

An orthogonal diagonalization is negative definite exactly when no coefficient is positive or zero. Thus the positive and null indices vanish, the negative counterpart of [Mathlib’s inertia definitions and Sylvester theorem](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Signature.lean#L65). At rank zero both sides remain true. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L319) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L312) passes.
The negative root example has signature (0,0,1).
That example is negative definite.

By [Mathlib’s inertia definitions and Sylvester theorem](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Signature.lean#L65), zero null and negative indices leave only positive coefficients in an orthogonal diagonalization, precisely positive definiteness. The null condition excludes degenerate semidefinite forms; no positive-rank assumption is needed. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RankOne/Basic.lean#L178) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L342) passes.
Positive rank one has signature (1,0,0).
The semidefinite affine example has a nonzero null index.

The lattice form is already symmetric, so its bundled semidefiniteness predicate reduces exactly to B(x,x)≥0 for every rational x. This is the elementwise convention in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3), with no restriction to integral carrier vectors or nonzero vectors. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L329) passes.
The affine model has nonnegative self-pairings despite degeneracy.

Expanding positivity of−B(x,x) gives B(x,x)<0 for each nonzero x. This is exactly the negative-definite convention in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3); the sign and nonzero restriction are both retained. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RankOne/Basic.lean#L204) passes.
The rank-one family gives exactly the expected negative parameter condition.

Evaluating the associated quadratic map gives Q(x)=B(x,x), so its strict positivity condition is exactly the displayed universal inequality. This is the positive-definite convention in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3), on the rational ambient space and with zero excluded. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RankOne/Basic.lean#L196) passes.
In rank one the condition is equivalent to a>0.

Pulling the identity-component ideal of H/I back along H→H/I cuts out N° inside the original ambient group, matching [Milne, Proposition 1.34](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=28). Published [subgroup-containment](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/IdentityComponent.lean#L64) and [tangent-retention](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/IdentityComponent.lean#L145) controls pass. The component is selected by its idempotent, preserving scheme structure; no reduction, ambient connectedness or smoothness is assumed.
The identity component lies inside the original subgroup, with reversed ideal order.
Passing to the identity component preserves the full tangent Lie subalgebra, without reducing the group.

A coordinate lies in the ambient ideal of N° exactly when its class in H/I lies in N’s own component ideal, as in [Milne, Proposition 1.34](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=28). The published [restriction-map control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/IdentityComponent.lean#L97) passes. This is full ideal membership under the quotient map, including nilpotents, rather than vanishing only on rational points.
Ambient and internal component presentations commute with actual quotient coordinate maps.

Every function vanishing on N also vanishes on N°, yielding I≤I.identityComponent, the reversed ideal form of [Milne, Proposition 1.34](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=28). The published [connected-subgroup containment control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/IdentityComponent.lean#L71) passes. The inclusion is not an equality unless the subgroup is connected; no connectedness or smoothness hypothesis on the ambient group is imposed.
Every geometrically connected closed subgroup of N lies in N°.

If V(J)⊆V(I) is geometrically connected, its identity-containing image lies in V(I)°, precisely [Milne, Remark 2.39(b)](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=63). The published [connected-case control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Connected/Comultiplication.lean#L251) passes. Lean’s I≤J hypothesis has the correct reversed direction; connectedness belongs to H/J, and no connectedness of H/I or smoothness of either subgroup is needed.
The component ideal vanishes exactly when the group spectrum is connected.

Quotienting H by the inverse image of N’s component ideal equals quotienting H/I by that ideal, giving the coordinate algebra of [Milne, Proposition 1.34](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=28). The published [ambient-restriction control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/IdentityComponent.lean#L97) passes. The isomorphism preserves Hopf structure and actual quotient maps; it identifies full schemes, not merely homeomorphic spectra or equal rational-point sets.
Ambient and internal component presentations commute with actual quotient coordinate maps.

The component of the counit point is connected, and over the algebraically closed base this is geometric connectedness, as in [Milne, Proposition 1.34](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=28) and [Stacks, §33.7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0361). The published [actual-component range control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Connected/GroupScheme.lean#L211) passes. The quotient comparison transports this property to the ambient ideal construction without adding reducedness or smoothness.
The scheme inclusion has precisely the counit connected component as its topological image.

The identity component is the open-and-closed piece selected by an idempotent, so localization preserves the assumed smoothness of N. This uses [locality of smoothness](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01V4). The published [idempotent-localization control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Smooth/IdentityComponent.lean#L29) passes. Smoothness is required for H/I itself; the statement does not infer it for arbitrary closed subgroups of a smooth ambient group.
The explicit idempotent localization inherits smoothness from the original group.

Intersecting evaluation kernels over S produces the ideal of its reduced closed-subgroup closure, as in [Milne, §§1.46–1.48](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=31) and [Milne, Proposition 3.16](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=79). Published [identity-subgroup](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Vanishing.lean#L243) and [radicality](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Vanishing.lean#L135) controls pass. Subgroup multiplication and inversion give the Hopf laws; tensor separation over the field justifies the coideal condition without finite type or algebraic closedness.
The identity point subgroup has precisely the augmentation ideal as its closure ideal.
The intersection of field-valued evaluation kernels is radical.

Membership means that every evaluation at a point of S annihilates the coordinate, the kernel construction of [Milne, Proposition 3.16](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=79). The published [intersection-of-kernels control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Vanishing.lean#L128) passes. The quantifier ranges over the given subgroup’s elements; it neither tests all value algebras nor assumes S already equals the points of a closed subgroup.
The full underlying ideal is the intersection of the specified evaluation kernels.

After quotienting by the intersection of S-evaluation kernels, those same evaluations separate elements, expressing the schematic density in [Milne, §§1.46–1.48](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=31). The published [vanishing-membership control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Vanishing.lean#L106) passes. This needs no Nullstellensatz, finite type or algebraically closed field: an element vanishing at every original point is zero precisely because that common kernel was quotiented out.
Membership means every evaluation at an original subgroup point vanishes.

The underlying ideal is exactly the intersection of the evaluation kernels indexed by S, matching the coordinate closure construction in [Milne, Proposition 3.16](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=79). The published [radicality control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Vanishing.lean#L135) passes. This identifies the full ideal rather than only its zero locus; the subgroup contains the identity, so the family of evaluations is nonempty.
The intersection of field-valued evaluation kernels is radical.

Each evaluation kernel is radical because its target is the field k, and arbitrary intersections of radical ideals remain radical. This matches the reduced closure of [Milne, §§1.46–1.48](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=31). The published [reduced-quotient control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Vanishing.lean#L141) passes. Ambient H may contain nilpotents; they vanish under every evaluation and are killed in the closure quotient.
The closure coordinate quotient is reduced, even if the ambient algebra is not.

A quotient by a radical ideal is reduced, so the closure coordinate algebra has no nonzero nilpotents, matching [Milne, §§1.46–1.48](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=31). The published [original-point separation control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Vanishing.lean#L112) passes. Reducedness is established for H/vanishingIdeal(S), not H; no finite-type, algebraically closed or smoothness hypothesis is silently introduced.
Original subgroup evaluations separate the closure coordinate algebra.

I⊆vanishingIdeal(S) exactly says that every point of S annihilates I, so V(I) contains S. This is the closure minimality of [Milne, §§1.46–1.48](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=31). Published [trivial-subgroup](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Vanishing.lean#L243) and [triviality-reflection](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Vanishing.lean#L249) controls pass. Ideal inclusion is reversed from closed-subgroup inclusion; no equality between S and all points of its closure is claimed.
The identity point subgroup has precisely the augmentation ideal as its closure ideal.
Closure is the identity subgroup exactly when the original point subgroup is trivial.

The trivial point subgroup contains only the counit point, so its vanishing ideal is the counit kernel, namely augmentation, consistent with [Milne, §§1.46–1.48](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=31). The published [trivial-point-subgroup control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Vanishing.lean#L226) passes. The result holds over any field; the identity subgroup is represented by augmentation, whereas the zero ideal defines the whole ambient group.
The closed subgroup generated by the trivial point subgroup has only the identity rational point.

A subgroup with identity-scheme closure consists only of the identity, because every original point belongs to its closure; conversely the identity point has counit kernel. This agrees with [Milne, §§1.46–1.48](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=31). The published [identity-points control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Vanishing.lean#L226) passes. The equivalence detects triviality of S, not injectivity of the closure operation on arbitrary subgroups.
The closed subgroup generated by the trivial point subgroup has only the identity rational point.

For reduced finite-type H over algebraically closed k, every nonzero coordinate survives some k-valued evaluation by [Stacks, Hilbert Nullstellensatz](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00FV). Thus the common kernel of all rational points is zero; all three hypotheses are explicit, so this does not erase nilpotents or assert density over arbitrary fields.
Algebraically closed evaluations separate reduced finite-type coordinates, with all hypotheses visible.

The construction retains nonreduced structure and works over arbitrary commutative base rings, without smoothness or finite type.
The actual quotient coordinate map gives a closed immersion of underlying schemes.
The inverse classification recovers the full defining ideal from its quotient closed subgroup.

Forgetting the closed-immersion proof leaves exactly the subobject represented by Spec(H/I)→Spec(H), the inclusion in [Milne, Proposition 3.15](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=79). The published [ideal-order control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Scheme/Classification.lean#L87) passes. Subobject.mk identifies presentations isomorphic over the ambient group; this equality does not replace the scheme by its underlying set or its rational-point subgroup.
Inclusion of quotient subgroup schemes is exactly reversed ideal inclusion.

V(I)⊆V(J) as closed subgroup schemes exactly when J⊆I, the order reversal in [Milne, Proposition 3.15](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=79). The converse recovers the actual coordinate factorization through fully faithful Hopf spectrum, so it detects full ideals, including nilpotents, rather than only their radicals.
The inverse classification recovers the full defining ideal from its quotient closed subgroup.

A coinduced topology from a locally connected space is locally connected. The quotient of a locally connected space by its connected components is discrete. Each singleton in the quotient pulls back to an open component, and the quotient topology reflects this openness. The binary product of preconnected spaces is preconnected in the product topology. It suffices to connect each point of s to one fixed x inside a preconnected subset of s. These subsets have a common point, giving the connected-fan argument.
